# $crav1-record-approval

lane: cross-cutting | group: Meetings and open questions | starter: no | stage: stable | since: 1.141.0 | prompts: 2
purpose: Record a named person's yes on an Approval needed item, after accept in this run.
use_when: You have a person's yes to record on an Approval needed item
reads: Reads `## Approval needed`, `## Constraints`, and `tasks.md` for the spec the user named.
writes: After `accept` in this run, appends one `Approved:` line under that item. The script is `scripts/approval_needed.py write --yes`. It keeps the file's line endings.
leaves alone: Leaves the item, `Person:`, `Holds:`, `Asked:`, `Pending:`, the constraint, plan, tasks, code, and every other spec line alone. Sends nothing. Does not apply. Does not commit.
limits: No item, or two items, stops and lists them. It does not invent an item. A headless run without `accept` stops and does not write. It names `$crav1-build-tasks` for the tasks it unblocks and does not run it. It is not a starter option.
flow:
- **`$crav1-record-approval`** shows the `Approved:` line, the constraint that still asks for the yes, and the tasks that line unblocks.
- It writes the line only after `accept` in that run.
- The line is `Approved: <person>, <source date>, <source>, "<quote>" (accepted by <recorder> <date>)` under `## Approval needed`.
- A live `apply` still needs the user's own yes in the build run.
- the spec folder command is `<interpreter> -X utf8 <skill crav1-tasks-ready-to-build>/scripts/resolve_spec.py "<query>" --root docs/specs`.
- `show` and `write` pass `--root`, `--person`, `--source-date`, `--source`, `--quote`, `--recorder`, and `--accepted`.
- `write` also passes `--yes`.
- On Windows `<interpreter>` is `python` with `PYTHONUTF8=1`.
- Elsewhere it is `python3`.

## Choice words
- question: Write the line
  - `accept`: write the Approved line shown in this run
called_by: Called by the user.
runs by itself: Calls no skill.
you run next: $crav1-build-tasks; $crav1-finalize-commit
first: `$crav1-record-approval Person: <who> Source: <link, or mail, or meeting> <date> Quote: "<their words>"`
walkthrough: from-record-approval.md
human: https://github.com/Crav1on/crav1-spec-kit/blob/v1.204.0/docs/reference/skills/crav1-record-approval.md
